subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP unsupported success claims be handled as a core source-turn invariant, a plugin API correlation seam plus ClawHub policy plugin, or folded into the broader final-delivery policy work?
rationale: Current main has hook and warning surfaces but no maintainer-approved rule for blocking or revising visible success claims that are not backed by side-effect evidence.

options.title: Define a narrow core invariant
options.body: Make source-channel turns expose a structured unsupported-claim or delivery outcome when visible completion claims lack matching tool-side-effect evidence.

options.title: Confirm plugin scope
options.body: Close the core item only after maintainers confirm current hooks can reliably correlate the final answer, tool ledger, and outbound delivery for a plugin implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader policy work
options.body: Track this under the broader final-delivery and tool-failure issues, accepting that Telegram-specific false-completion handling waits for that product decision.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core invariant
recommendation.body: Make source-channel turns expose a structured unsupported-claim or delivery outcome when visible completion claims lack matching tool-side-effect evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete made the adjacent ClawHub/plugin scope decision in #68051 and the remaining question is the same core-versus-plugin policy boundary.
